name: Anti-consumerism
summary: Anti-consumerism opposes a social and economic order in which people are encouraged to acquire goods beyond need or to display status. Its most developed themes are criticism of advertising, the ecological cost of overconsumption, voluntary simplicity, and doubts that growth or green technology alone can fix this. It is a cultural and ethical critique more than a full political programme, so it has little to say on many questions of state and regime.
scope: Modern anti-consumerism as a loose movement: Thoreau's Walden, Veblen's critique of conspicuous consumption, voluntary simplicity (Gregg, Elgin), Naomi Klein's No Logo, Stiegler, and the degrowth current. Excludes narrowly religious asceticism and primitivism; most answers on matters outside consumption and economy are inferred and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Henry David Thoreau
keyFigures.role: Author of Walden, whose experiment in simple living is a founding text of the tradition.

keyFigures.name: Thorstein Veblen
keyFigures.role: Economist who analysed conspicuous consumption in The Theory of the Leisure Class (1899).

keyFigures.name: Naomi Klein
keyFigures.role: Author of No Logo (2000), a key anti-corporate, anti-brand work.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never a core theme; adherents on the left of the movement favour public provision of basic needs, inferred from its focus on needs over wants.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Adherents split: some want fair pay, others want less dependence on wage income and spending altogether, so the issue is not defining.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement blames profit-driven markets for manufacturing wants and ignoring public good, though some Austrian-leaning critics dissent.

public-ownership.rationale: Anti-consumerism targets consumption culture rather than ownership forms; adherents range from socialists to localists.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Veblen's critique of conspicuous consumption by the rich suggests sympathy for taxing luxury wealth, but taxation is not discussed as doctrine.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; unions can be seen as defending wages that fund consumption or as protecting workers, so adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Thoreau warns of possessions as fetters; adherents treat property as less sacred than a life of sufficiency, an inference.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Concern centres on firms pursuing profit at public expense, and adherents favour curbs such as limits on advertising.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not a theme; the stress on sufficiency over accumulation makes cuts unattractive, inferred from the focus on needs.

worker-ownership.rationale: Some strands (commoning, cooperatives) favour it but it is not central to the consumption critique.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's anti-corporate, autonomy-minded outlook suggests wariness of surveillance, including data harvested for targeting ads.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from libertarian to health-minded abstainers.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; no common line.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grassroots, culture-jamming and community orientation, which favours bottom-up change.

state-harmful.rationale: Anti-consumerism is not anti-state; many adherents want policy such as ad limits and degrowth measures, so they reject abolition.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from simple-living, anti-war and anti-materialist associations; not a stated position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; commodification critiques cut both ways.

decide-locally.rationale: Simple-living and ecovillage strands prize small-scale, local community, though not stated as a rule.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents include religious traditionalists and secular progressives; the movement itself is neutral.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split across religious and secular camps.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious figures like Francis and Gandhi inspire it, but secular strands are equally prominent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; no common line.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement opposes cultural homogenisation by globalised brands, but it is not nationalist; adherents are split.

gradual-change.rationale: Culture jamming and demands for a break with consumer society suggest impatience, but this is inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anti-globalisation links suggest suspicion of distant institutions, inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The movement is tied to anti-globalisation and objects to globalised corporate trade and cultural homogenisation.

nation-first.rationale: Not nationalist; the anti-globalisation strand favours local over national or global, so this reads as rejection, inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military intervention is outside the consumption critique, and adherents hold no shared line.

limit-growth.rationale: The degrowth and steady-state current in the scope holds that overconsumption drives ecological damage, but the only source is the degrowth article and branding-focused critics such as Klein do not target growth itself.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Overconsumption is seen as a root of climate change and adherents want consumption cut, not left to green tech alone.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sources say green technology alone cannot solve consumption-driven problems; Thoreau warned men become tools of their tools.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Adherents divide between pro-nuclear and anti-nuclear environmentalists; the ideology is silent.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mostly reformist and lifestyle-based; some radicals differ, so split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the grassroots, community orientation of the movement.

central-planning.rationale: Degrowth stresses democratic decision-making rather than command planning, an inference for the wider movement.

socialized-markets.rationale: Adherents divide between market socialism, commoning and a general doubt of markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is not part of the consumption critique; no sourced position on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Veblen's critique of inherited leisure class wealth leans this way, but it is not a stated anti-consumerist programme.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is a common degrowth proposal; extending it to anti-consumerism as a whole is an inference.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Opposes globalised trade but protectionism is not an anti-consumerist programme.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between state and local control.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Thoreau and simple-living thought favour small-scale independence over concentrated wealth, inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mainstream anti-consumerism wants reduced consumption, not abolition of money; only radical strands go further.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Austrian-leaning critics and others differ; no common line.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Foreign to the movement's grassroots outlook.

one-party-rule.rationale: Opposed to authoritarian rule given its community, democratic and culture-jamming orientation, inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The critique concerns consumption, not forms of head of state, so adherents are indifferent.

democracy-best.rationale: Degrowth emphasises democratic decision-making, though the ideology as a whole says little about regime type.

direct-votes.rationale: Degrowth favours deliberative and participatory forums, an inference for the broader movement.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; some radicals favour them, most do not.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is unrelated to the critique of consumer culture; adherents are not united on it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Gandhian and religious roots (Gregg, Gandhi) lean nonviolent; some radicals dissent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Simple-living is associated with anti-war movements.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religious figures inspire it but it does not seek scriptural law, inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from distrust of profit-driven provision of public goods.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not ethnic nationalist; opposes homogenisation but not on ethnic terms, inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Some adherents are Marxists, but Marxists also criticise anti-consumerism; split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; sympathetic strands exist but no doctrine.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism are not addressed in the movement's sources, and adherents vary.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Thoreau and the religious tradition treat acquisitive self-regard and wealth-chasing as the root of quiet desperation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from communitarian to libertarian.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Linked to deep ecology and harmony with nature in simple-living thought.

limit-population.rationale: Rees and Hern write on limits to growth, but population control is contested among adherents.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Critics call it anti-modern, but mainstream adherents seek reform of consumer culture rather than call all industrial civilisation a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Sources say technology alone is insufficient and the movement opposes ever-faster consumption cycles.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from rejection of consumer-culture promises of self-improvement through products.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred; Stiegler criticises technological capture of attention.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from wariness of data harvesting by corporations and states.

restore-past-order.rationale: Not restorationist; reform-oriented, though religious strands sometimes appeal to tradition.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement is value-driven but has no stated stance on pragmatism versus ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Culture jamming, subvertising and boycotts are characteristic tactics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Thoreau's practice of living the change and simple-living ethos suggest it, inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Simple living means fewer possessions, not abandonment of agriculture or settled life; only fringe primitivists dissent.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Emphasis on needs over wants fits, but distribution rules are not a theme; split.

production-for-use.rationale: Critique centres on profit-driven production creating artificial wants, favouring production for need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxists see it as ignoring this; the movement targets profit over public good without a theory of exploitation.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; some commoning strands might favour it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources link consumerism to waste and ecological harm, not to imperialism and great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Tax-resistance is associated with some simple-living strands, but the mainstream wants public policy.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want to restrict advertising, which cuts both ways.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual versus group rights is not a theme; adherents range from libertarian to communitarian.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from community and democratic emphasis.

state-as-business.rationale: Opposes treating public life as commerce; critics of consumer culture reject citizens-as-customers framing.

positive-liberty.rationale: The material-means view of freedom is not stated in the movement's sources, though critics of status competition might sympathise.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a stated view though media critique exists.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No basis in the ideology; inferred rejection.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist or communal representation is not discussed by the movement.

total-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grassroots and autonomy emphasis.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposed to coerced labour; Thoreau's emphasis on independence.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Postmodern strands accept it, but not a shared doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: Religious strands say yes, postmodern strands say no; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The movement criticises profit over the public good but takes no position on unitary versus plural politics.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism is outside the scope of the consumption critique.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rights are unrelated to the movement's concerns.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not addressed, though opposition to cultural homogenisation could lean sympathetic.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Degrowth calls for democratising economic relations.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not a theme; adherents differ on markets in schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Austrian-leaning critics oppose stimulating consumption but others differ; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred from scepticism of market-driven consumer society.

rule-by-example.rationale: The idea that rulers should govern by moral example is not stated in anti-consumerist sources, though simple-living ethics value personal example.

national-self-determination.rationale: National self-determination is not addressed; the movement is more local or global than national.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility for immigrants is not a topic in the movement.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Simple living seeks less time in paid work and basic-income style support; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on employer-worker relations; Marxists and others in the milieu disagree.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: No relation to doctrine; inferred rejection of novelty-for-its-own-sake that fashion represents (Thoreau).

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are a different tradition; anti-consumerism has no stated view.

workers-nation.rationale: The question of national versus international class organisation is not part of the ideology.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; critics note masculinity anxieties but the doctrine is neutral.

ban-interest.rationale: Some religious strands object to usury and debt, but not shared.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: No basis in the ideology; inferred rejection.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist theory of the state is not shared by the movement, and Marxists in fact criticise it.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Opposes overconsumption as a driver of climate change and resource depletion.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; opposes cultural homogenisation, but split.

elite-replacement.rationale: No basis in the ideology; inferred rejection.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not discussed by the movement.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from anti-globalisation and anti-war orientation.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender structure is not addressed in the core sources, aside from some feminist critiques of the movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Distrust of corporate power is central, but elites in politics are not the focus.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred rejection; no support in the ideology.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice for security-force abuses is outside the movement's scope.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Adherents want regulation of advertising and corporate conduct.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No basis in the ideology; inferred rejection.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Veblen-style critique of status display implies opposition to rank by wealth; not directly stated.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Debates about building socialism in one country belong to Marxism, not this movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is not covered by anti-consumerist sources.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal law and religion are not a theme in the movement.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from general liberal-pluralist stance of the movement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Animal-rights ties exist but a legal ban is not doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in schools is not addressed, and religious and secular adherents differ.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Degrowth's democratic emphasis, inferred for the broader movement.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export focus conflicts with the critique of production for its own sake, inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced minority removal has no support in the movement's sources, but the movement does not engage with it either, so this is a low-confidence rejection from its nonviolent roots.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Status competition is the target in Veblen's account of emulation, and the movement criticises competitive acquisition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not part of the movement's concerns.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed, though advertising seen as manipulation fits partly.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed in anti-consumerist sources.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Emphasis on needs over wants and critiques of status competition suggest sympathy, but not a doctrine.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy of this kind is not addressed; asset-owning could appeal to some, but others see it as consumerism.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred; the movement blames consumption systems rather than population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: No basis in the ideology; inferred rejection.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the movement's sources, though participatory strands might sympathise.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civil-libertarian leaning.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not a stated anti-consumerist policy; adherents are split on market intervention.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposed to controlled media; adherents criticise corporate control of media and advertising and would not substitute state control.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are unrelated to the consumption critique.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the anti-status, anti-wealth-display stance.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a topic; the movement is mostly non-party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Anti-globalisation link makes this doubtful, inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the movement, though religious voices inspire it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Religious figures inspire it but it does not seek clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist-Leninist position, not part of anti-consumerism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Culture-jamming and satirical art such as Banksy imply free expression; adherents worry about commercial culture, not state censorship.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not addressed, though anti-war sympathies might lean toward ending them.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry is not an anti-consumerist idea.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a doctrine; Thoreau discusses owning housing but not banning rent.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Thoreau and simple-living tradition favour life close to nature, though not a modern doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not a concern of the movement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement has no stated view on the educated classes, though some critics call it elitist.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Opposes homogenisation, but no stated view on ranking.

death-penalty.rationale: Gandhian and religious pacifist lineage, inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula on sex and gender are outside the movement's scope.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the movement's environmental, science-informed concerns.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Commodification critiques cut both ways; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is unrelated to the consumption critique.

minority-language-support.rationale: Opposes cultural homogenisation by global brands, so supports linguistic diversity by inference.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for religious practice are not addressed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Thoreau decries fashion-following and conformity; the movement values authentic living apart from consumer norms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Poor-country debt relief is not specifically addressed, though anti-globalisation links might sympathise.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Post-colonial economic transformation is not a theme of this movement.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Growth is the target of the critique, so growth cannot justify restrictions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; adherents want less consumption in rich countries but aid is a separate matter.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Executive selection is not a topic of the movement.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed, and adherents range from Austrian to left views.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims in peace deals are unrelated to the movement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Concern for public good over profit suggests this, though not explicitly stated.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Classification of the USSR is a Marxist debate outside this movement.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental concern and doubts that technology solves problems support acting before certainty.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees such as NATO's are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is unrelated to the movement's concerns.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state hierarchy is not a theme of anti-consumerism.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not addressed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Sources say advertising and culture shape wants and the self, so character is formed by surroundings.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not part of the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from rejection of mass-culture image-making and display.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the movement's concerns.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist theory not engaged by anti-consumerism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not a stated aim; Thoreau-style smallholding might sympathise, but the movement has no programme on estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not discussed in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism has no basis in the movement, and its anti-nationalist, anti-war leanings imply opposition, but it is never addressed directly.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious freedom is not directly addressed, though the movement draws on voluntary, conscience-based ethics, so rejection is inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress laws are not addressed; opposition is inferred from the movement's emphasis on personal autonomy and its critique of coercion.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed, and anti-globalisation sentiment pulls against it while others are indifferent.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Strategy for persecuted minorities falls outside the movement.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not an anti-consumerist tenet, and Marxists dispute the movement's emphasis on values and culture.

ban-cartels.rationale: Concern about concentrated corporate power suggests support.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed; adherents who dislike corporate power and those who dislike public subsidy of firms differ.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review versus majoritarianism is not discussed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Representation quotas are not addressed in the movement's sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Simple living favours self-sufficiency at the household and local level, but not autarkic blocs with colonies.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anti-globalisation and environmental strands favour binding standards on trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: Thoreau values meaning over material gain in Walden, from which a preference for non-material motives to work is inferred; no source proposes replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Opposed to violent minority action; Gandhian roots.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Veblen's critique of leisure-class status supports it, inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History curriculum content is not a concern of the movement.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage is not discussed; rejection is inferred from the movement's opposition to cultural homogenisation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is not addressed in the movement's sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the core doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Some say consumerism can be separated from capitalism, others not; split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy influence is not addressed; rejection is inferred from its anti-globalisation and anti-hegemony leanings.

delink-world-market.rationale: Degrowth strands are sympathetic, but the broader movement is not committed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist thesis is not part of anti-consumerism, though some critiques of rich-world consumption echo it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not a topic of the movement.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty law is not discussed.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus decision rules are not addressed, though some communitarian strands practise consensus.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance doctrine is not stated, though Thoreau's civil disobedience tradition leans this way, mixed with pacifist caution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty is outside the movement's concerns.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Anti-consumerism is commonly linked with animal rights.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal-rights links push against, but simple-living adherents farm; split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Opposes display of wealth but not framed as an obligation; split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Thoreau withdrew to Walden, yet the movement is also actively political; split.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Stiegler and others argue advertising and media damage development and sustain consumption.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not stated, but critiques of advertising and mass media resemble it, so adherents split on the framing.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the movement, which addresses consumption in rich countries more than extraction.

native-born-offices.rationale: Eligibility for public office is not addressed.

party-own-road.rationale: Intra-communist autonomy is not relevant to this movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Simple living values self-reliance, but not as national aid policy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial revanchism is not addressed; rejection is inferred from the movement's anti-war leanings.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political authority is not addressed in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional values like anti-fascism are not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparative totalitarianism is outside the movement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical dispute with no connection to the movement; rejection is inferred from its general egalitarian ethics.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not addressed by the movement, though one feminist critique ties its rhetoric to masculinity anxieties.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is unrelated to the consumption critique.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Civilisational relativism about political forms is not stated, though adherents oppose cultural homogenisation.

paid-care-work.rationale: Degrowth's four-in-one model values care work, but payment is not a common view.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duties are not addressed, though religious and traditional strands value them.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service selection is not part of the movement.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of strategic firms is not specifically addressed, though anti-globalisation sentiment might lean sympathetic.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is outside the movement's concerns.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from distrust of financial markets.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; commoning strands might agree.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, grassroots outlook; the ideology does not address the rule of law directly.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Voluntary simplicity and the critique of conspicuous consumption (Veblen, Thoreau) hold that consumer culture is wasteful and harmful to people and society.

single-official-language.rationale: Anti-consumerism is a cultural critique of consumption with no language policy, and adherents are not united on it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; localist and degrowth strands might favour local land control while cosmopolitan simplicity movements would not, so adherents are split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The movement does not address racial discrimination; its left wing is sympathetic to outcome-based equity but this is not a defining position.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The movement has no foreign-policy doctrine, but its simple-living and degrowth currents are generally pacifist; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed directly; the pacifist and anti-hegemonic leanings of voluntary simplicity and degrowth suggest opposition to forcible intervention, inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Advertising and corporate marketing are the movement's main targets, so adherents see business power over public life as excessive.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; no common position.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Degrowth and simple-living strands see population and consumption growth as environmental pressures; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localist and community-minded strands favour keeping housing for residents; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Degrowth strands favour public work and shorter hours over market growth; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: No stated position on democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Thoreau-style individualism holds that conscience outranks law as such; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement's small-scale, local focus leans to non-interference abroad; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not an anti-consumerist issue.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement's critique is aimed at consumer culture and business, not minorities; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Voluntary simplicity favours small, decentralised, voluntary groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; no stated position.

religious-nation.rationale: Religion is not a defining theme and the movement is non-nationalist; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Voluntary simplicity keeps modest personal belongings while criticising accumulation and status goods; sympathy for common ownership of productive means is inferred, and the movement is not explicitly socialist.

socialized-care.rationale: No stated position; degrowth favours shared services and communal living but the movement as a whole does not address housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The movement has no interest in language policy; its stress on pluralism and voluntary choice suggests mild opposition to compulsory purging. Inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no position on treaties between governments and internal nations; the issue is not defining.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Simple living and degrowth favour small, cooperative, self-governing communities, though the movement does not require common ownership; inferred, with Thoreau as an individualist counterexample.

majority-settlement.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no position on settlement policy; the issue is not defining.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anti-consumerism criticises consumer capitalism without endorsing state communism, and degrowth presents itself as an alternative path; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; indifferent.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as rejection of denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's liberal and libertarian tendencies in social matters.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's emphasis on freedom, voluntary simplicity and civic engagement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's secular, voluntary character.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from critiques of corporate power.

property-franchise.rationale: Nothing in anti-consumerism supports wealth-limited voting and its egalitarian streak opposes it; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Degrowth and ecofeminist currents link exploitation of nature and women, but it is not central; inferred.

reification.rationale: Veblen and Stiegler describe how market society shapes desires and relations through things, though Marx's term is not the movement's own.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anti-consumerism criticises corporate media and advertising control of public attention; inferred, not a statement on press freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no position on legal procedure; inferred neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement has no racial doctrine and is broadly egalitarian; inferred rejection.

online-participation.rationale: Views are split between digital activism and critique of screen-driven consumption; no source addresses it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Unrelated to consumption; inferred rejection from its liberal and egalitarian leanings.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anti-consumerist boycotts target corporations over conduct, not owners' religion; inferred disagreement.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anti-consumerism and degrowth favour participatory democracy so citizens can set limits on consumption; inferred, not a stated demand.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement is mostly secular or spiritual-agnostic and has no position on reinterpreting religious law; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Veblen's critique of conspicuous consumption and the movement's concern with wealth-driven status display imply that extreme wealth distorts society, though liberty is not its own framing.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a cultural critique with no stated position on military service, but its mostly progressive adherents would accept equal treatment.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: the critique targets consumption, not religion, and voluntary simplicity has strong religious and spiritual roots, so state atheism promotion is unlikely to be endorsed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Adherents split: the movement is silent on policing, and anarchist strands favour abolition while most simplicity advocates do not discuss it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement has no position on constitutional design for divided societies; nothing in its sources addresses it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: voluntary simplicity and community self-reliance favour local mutual aid, though degrowth adherents also want public provision of basic needs.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents show no consistent view on political term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no source discusses liquid democracy, and its participatory strands might be sympathetic.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Adherents split: ecological concern favours long-term risk reduction, but the movement focuses on overconsumption rather than extinction risk and often distrusts technology-led priorities.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the movement's mostly progressive and secular adherents would favour equal eligibility, but religion is outside its scope.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the movement's egalitarian outlook; marital authority is not a theme in its sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The degrowth and localist strand favours deeper local democracy; inferred, not a stated anti-consumerist demand.

rent-control.rationale: Degrowth thinkers favour decommodifying basic needs such as housing; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Klein-style critique of brand and corporate power inclines adherents against intellectual-property monopolies; inferred and weakly held.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Degrowth and simple living favour demilitarisation; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no position on state recognition of historical atrocities.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Veblen's critique of the leisure class treats income from ownership without useful work as parasitic and wasteful.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Simple living has pacifist strands but no doctrine against lethal self-defence; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Thoreau's individualism distrusts collective national myths; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on the social construction of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on feminist politics.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Thoreau and the simplicity tradition distrust public glorification of sacrifice; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anti-consumerism is a cultural and ethical critique, not a spiritual-war politics; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on homelands or diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on whether culture or the state comes first.

god-not-male.rationale: Simple living includes religious and secular strands with no common position on language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Simple living includes religious and secular strands with no common position on judging scripture.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement's concern is with consumption, not ethnic economic control, and it leans toward universal values; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no doctrine on administrative borders.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from its critique of corporate power and labour exploitation, as in No Logo; no stated position.

person-over-state.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Its central claim is that fulfilment lies beyond material acquisition, as in Thoreau and voluntary simplicity.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of corporate technological fixes and agribusiness; no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the ecological case for smaller footprints and lower consumption, which dense living supports.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: it is a critique of consumption with no racial programme, and its universalist ethic runs against racial blocs.

racial-pride.rationale: The ideology has no stated position on this, and adherents are split, so it is left neutral.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from its general opposition to waste and resource competition; no stated position.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is a cultural critique of consumption with no doctrine on nationhood.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses shared ethical life over group divisions and offers no case for separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the movement is cosmopolitan and focused on corporate and cultural power, not foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: the left of the movement and degrowth favour public provision of basic needs, education included.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: degrowth and green anti-consumerists support taxes on resource use and pollution, though some prefer caps and regulation.

future-generations.rationale: The ecological cost of overconsumption is a developed theme, and degrowth stresses sustaining the planet for those to come.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; some ecofeminist-leaning adherents say yes, but it is no core claim.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the critique of waste and of consumption-driven economies; not a stated theme.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic and anti-corporate leanings; not a stated theme.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Voluntary simplicity and Thoreau stress individuals and communities choosing their own way of living and producing, without a fixed blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anti-consumerism and degrowth criticise reducing nature to market value and treating it as a growth resource.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: the movement focuses on consumption, not national community, and criticises status-seeking collective identity; not stated.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: opposition to debt-financed consumption and credentialism suggests sympathy, but it is not a stated theme.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split on regional exploitation analysis, so left neutral.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: Thoreau and simplicity writers appeal to genuine human needs, but the movement states no view on a fixed human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the critique of advertising favours media free of commercial control; not a stated policy.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The movement draws on both religious and secular simplicity traditions and takes no stand on religious truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not a theme; adherents favour local and small-scale farming but have no agreed view on price supports.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of acquisition and waste and its peace-leaning simplicity tradition; never a stated programme.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: the critique of the commercial order leads many adherents to want a political voice for working people, but there is no party programme.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the general left-leaning humane outlook; FGM is not addressed by the movement.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from equality and fairness principles; the movement itself does not address inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not a concern of the movement.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Adherents want stronger limits on polluting overconsumption, but the choice of tort liability against agency regulation is not a stated position.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: No stated position; the movement's respect for traditional simple living does not imply a view on chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Degrowth and the critique of overconsumption put ecological limits above unlimited consumer freedom, though the movement stresses voluntary choice.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between a liberal dislike of harsh sentencing and a general interest in social order.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split between cosmopolitan and localist leanings.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the movement's left-leaning strands favour organised labour and collective protection of workers, so a right-to-work ban on union security is more likely opposed.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a cultural critique with no settled position on electoral administration, and adherents split between access and integrity concerns.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: a movement valuing simplicity and pluralism has no stake in privileging one religious interpretation, and its liberal-leaning adherents would accept equal recognition.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: degrowth and simplicity writers stress democratic participation, but the statement's 'whatever policies' clause is a procedural minimum most would accept rather than a stated position.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: the movement says little about sexual morality, and its mostly liberal adherents accept it; Walden-style asceticism is a personal ethic, not a rule for others.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: the movement's ethos of openness, civil liberties and local self-reliance makes cutting communications for order unlikely to be endorsed, though it is not discussed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: degrowth strands favour universal public provision or basic income over means-tested cash replacing welfare, but the specific design is not discussed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: the movement is liberal-egalitarian in outlook and none of its thinkers argue against women's political equality.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no stated view; simplicity and degrowth writers focus on consumption, and adherents range from secular to religious ascetics.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: the mostly progressive adherents accept the mainstream scientific view, though race is outside the movement's concerns.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: left-leaning adherents of degrowth generally support public equality measures, but this is not a theme of the movement.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Thoreau defended property gained by work, but the movement has no stated first-claim doctrine and the degrowth current favours commons; inferred and split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anti-consumerism is a cultural critique with no stated view on international courts; inferred as indifferent.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The movement draws on secular and varied sources, and the profile excludes narrowly religious asceticism; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Sources show no doctrine on self-government arrangements; inferred as indifferent.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Degrowth and simplicity favour decentralised, democratic economies over bureaucratic planned states; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Degrowth favours democratic participation, but the movement has no stated view on indirect election; inferred and split.

national-church-status.rationale: Anti-consumerism's secular critique gives no support for church privilege; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement has no stated position on territorial autonomy; inferred as indifferent.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Anti-consumerism does not address territorial disputes; inferred as indifferent.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: No source connects anti-consumerism to borders; inferred as indifferent.

simple-living.rationale: Voluntary simplicity is central, urging fewer possessions, limited needs and self-sufficiency, as Thoreau advised in Walden.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The movement does not address settlement policy; inferred as indifferent.

equal-conscription.rationale: Sources show no stance on conscription; inferred as indifferent.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Adherents are split and the critique of consumption says nothing about national ties to land; inferred from its focus on consumption.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: An ethical critique of the social order, not a regime programme; inferred humane opposition to killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anti-consumerism has no foreign-policy line; inferred as indifferent.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement is not nationalist and does not address kin minorities; adherents are not defined by this issue.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the degrowth and commons-oriented strand, which treats resources as shared rather than private to first claimants.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Thoreau's emphasis on personal autonomy and refusing to be bound to others' ends, though the movement is not libertarian.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: degrowth thinkers favour discouraging consumption, so cutting taxes on purchases runs against the grain, though necessities are a partial exception.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Left-leaning adherents favour public provision of needs, others favour simple voluntary living; not a defining issue.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grassroots, civil-society character; it works through campaigns and groups rather than leader-to-people rule.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from criticism of corporate power and marketing influence in the consumer order, as in No Logo.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The movement does not address religious politics; adherents are split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Adherents split between technological optimists in degrowth and those favouring a simpler, low-tech life; no common line.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's mostly liberal, left-leaning outlook; it is not a topic the sources discuss.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; degrowth concerns global resource use rather than who holds sovereignty over it.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Anti-consumerists judge wealth by its social cost and the wastefulness of conspicuous display, not only by how it was acquired; inferred from Veblen.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Degrowth and anti-corporate critics favour levies that curb speculation and raise public money; inferred, not a core anti-consumerist demand.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anti-consumerism is not about race, but its critics of capitalism usually accept that racism is still a major obstacle; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Thoreau's civil disobedience tradition holds that individual conscience can override unjust laws; inferred from Walden-era thought as the sources here treat consumption.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Degrowth links lower consumption to shorter paid work, but anti-consumerists are wary of technology-driven consumption, so support is partial; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Anti-consumerism says nothing about the distribution of global power; adherents are not aligned on it.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Veblen and Thoreau did not rest their critique on a labour theory of value; some strands do and others do not.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Anti-consumerism is not tied to patriotism either way; the movement is mostly indifferent to national feeling.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anti-consumerists mostly care about lifestyle and culture rather than wages alone, and rank consumption critique above material growth; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Degrowth and simple living favour decentralised, small-scale economies, not party-directed market growth; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Advertising aimed at the public should be strictly limited by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Advertising is the most developed anti-consumerist theme, criticised for equating happiness with possessions and for intrusive public ads.

missingStatements.text: People should deliberately reduce what they own and buy, even if they could afford more.
missingStatements.rationale: Voluntary simplicity is central, urging fewer possessions and lower spending, as Thoreau advised.

missingStatements.text: Buying expensive goods mainly to display status is wasteful and harms society.
missingStatements.rationale: Veblen's conspicuous consumption and emulation argument holds such display is wasteful and drives status competition.

missingStatements.text: Working hours should be reduced so that people need and earn less.
missingStatements.rationale: Simple living and degrowth both link lower consumption to less paid work and more time for other pursuits.
missingStatements.declined: Hours reduction is a degrowth and labour-policy position more than a core anti-consumerist claim, and is not captured by a clean neutral statement without bloating the bank.

notes: Anti-consumerism is a cultural critique that can sit alongside socialist, Gandhian, religious, localist or even Austrian-economics views, so many non-economic answers are 0 or low confidence. Marxists and libertarians both criticise it.
